title: P0: Egress path degradation — after-action and runbook draft
impact_summary: A regional egress path degradation in us-west-2 caused sustained high p95/p99 latency across streamed responses and a wave of intermittent 5xxs for hosted-api streaming endpoints. Customer-visible impact: ~18% of streaming sessions experienced fragmentation or reconnects; non-streaming RPCs saw elevated tail latency but lower error rate. Several high-throughput tenants reported increased token costs due to retransmits and retries.
content:
Overview:
On 2029-10-12 at ~03:14 UTC we started seeing a sharp rise in streaming session partial writes and client reconnects originating from the us-west-2 edge cluster. The symptoms included: persistent p95/p99 token latency increases (streaming chunks delayed by 200-800ms), spikes in application-level 502/503 for stream-write operations, and a downstream cache pressure cascade (kv-cache eviction rate up 4x).

This doc is an after-action and a runbook draft for handling similar egress path degradations. It contains a short timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations taken during the incident, proposed long-term fixes, and specific runbook changes to add to the hosted-api incident runbook.

Timeline (high level):
- 03:14 UTC: First alert from synthetic stream-health probe (p99 chunk latency > 250ms) and elevated reconnect rate from edge->ingress metrics. Pager triggered.
- 03:18 UTC: Oncall confirms customer Slack reports and dashboards show correlated token retransmit increase.
- 03:28 UTC: Initial mitigation: route traffic away from affected egress subnet by flipping edge-egress-balance policy (manual drift to next-egress). Partial improvement but not full.
- 03:35 UTC: SRE teams run packet captures at edge1 and edge2; observe elevated retransmit rates and TCP keepalive resets on connections crossing a particular ISP egress hop.
- 04:05 UTC: Network team escalates to cloud provider support — suspected transient BGP / fabric flap affecting one egress region.
- 04:40 UTC: Autoscaler misreaction observed: streaming autoscaler detected perceived latency and added capacity, which increased KV cache churn and amplified backend write fanout. Scaling was paused and later limited by manual override.
- 05:10 UTC: Full traffic shift to alternate egress and region-level routing fallback applied; streaming chunk error rate dropped ~75% within 8 minutes.
- 07:02 UTC: Provider confirms BGP flap resolved and we gradually rebalanced traffic back to standard routing. Incident declared resolved.

Root cause (summary):
Primary cause: transient egress path degradation (fabric/BGP flap) in us-west-2 provider edge resulting in increased packet loss and retransmits for sessions that used a small set of provider egress IPs. This manifested as higher latency for streaming chunk ACKs and increased client reconnects.
Contributing factors:
- Edge routing policy pinned a subset of high-throughput customers to the affected egress IPs for performance isolation; this amplified customer impact.
- Streaming autoscaler reacted to increased p95 latency by provisioning more backends without awareness of upstream packet loss, which increased concurrency and KV-cache churn, amplifying tail effects.
- Runbook lacked a quick checklist to identify provider-level egress issues vs internal service regressions; early mitigation steps were slow (first traffic shift was manual and partial).

Immediate mitigations (actions taken during incident):
1) Traffic shift: we diverted traffic from the affected egress IP block to alternate egress nodes/regions using the edge-egress-balance override. This provided the largest immediate improvement.
2) Autoscaler hold: placed a temporary hard cap on streaming autoscaler decisions while stabilization occurred to avoid thrash.
3) Increased telemetry granularity: temporarily increased sampling for tcp retransmit metrics and edge packet loss telemetry to diagnose the failure domain.
4) Customer comms: CS posted a status update referencing intermittent streaming fragmentation while we investigated; major customers were given targeted ETA updates.

Why mitigations helped: diverting to different egress paths avoided the problematic provider hop. Capping autoscaler reduced cache thrash and allowed existing sessions to complete. Enhanced telemetry made it possible to pinpoint the egress-layer as the common failure surface.

Why we were slow / where process failed:
- Detection signal: the initial alerting relied on application-layer streaming chunk latency; we do not have a separate early egress-loss alert path.
- Playbook coverage: our playbook prioritized internal memory or scheduler regressions; it did not include provider-egress checks (BGP/ISP path) or a one-click region fallback.
- Escalation: routing provider contact and confirmation took ~1h due to routing ownership ambiguity between edge/network and cloud-platform teams.

Runbook draft additions (short):
- New section: "Egress fabric degradation" with quick checks:
  * Check: edge.tcp.retransmit.rate by edge node and egress-ip
  * Check: provider BGP session status via cloud provider console (if available)
  * Check: edge-egress-balance distribution and pinned traffic policies
  * Quick mitigation: run `edgectl routing override --egress-set alternate-usw2 --duration 30m` (templated command)
  * If autoscaler activity > threshold during ongoing packet loss, run `infra-scaler-safeguard --lock streaming --owner sRE-oncall`
- Add: who-to-call list (cloud provider network ops escalation path + internal edge routing owners) and expected SLAs for provider acknowledgement.

Long-term engineering actions (initial list):
- Short-term (2–4 weeks):
  * Add egress loss detection alert that correlates tcp retransmits, provider flaps, and streaming reconnect rate (owner: Jin Soo).
  * Add an automated, reversible traffic fallback play that can shift a percentage of traffic away from suspect egress IPs with staged rollback (owner: Diego).
  * Add autoscaler safety gate: if packet loss or retransmit rate exceeds X, autoscaler should pause scaling and signal SRE (owner: Ben).
- Medium-term (1–3 months):
  * Rework edge-egress-balancer to avoid tight pinning of heavy tenants to a small egress IP set; ensure diversity by default.
  * Implement KV-cache pressure backpressure signals so that backend scaling decisions take cache-eviction-rate into account.
- Long-term (3–6 months):
  * Work with provider to get persistent monitoring hooks for BGP/session flaps for our egress IP blocks (contract change).
  * Consider multi-provider egress for critical tenants (configuration and billing path).

Runbook concrete changes to merge (PR checklist):
- Add new alert definitions and playbook steps for egress fabric issues.
- Add templated commands and runbook escalation contact for provider network ops.
- Add a pre-baked traffic-fallback automation play (staged 10/30/60% shifts) with safety rollbacks.

Follow-ups and owners (action items):
- JIRA-ENG-9876 (Jin Soo): Add egress-loss alert and dashboard (due 2029-10-26).
- infra#1425 (Diego): Implement staged traffic fallback CLI + API (due 2029-11-09).
- oss#1590 (Ben): Autoscaler safety gate for packet loss signal (spec draft due 2029-10-20).
- Product/CS (Maya): Post-incident customer summary and FAQ update (due 2029-10-15).
- SRE (Aisha): Update hosted-api incident runbook with egress section and run the first tabletop within 2 weeks (due 2029-10-26).

Communication notes and customer impact detail:
- We documented affected customers (top three tenants by traffic) and provided targeted follow-ups. There were no data-loss reports and no authentication incidents. The primary customer pain was streaming truncation and increased token / retry cost.
- CS recommended retry-window tuning to customers as a temporary mitigation to reduce duplicate token cost until the path stabilized.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- What exact provider-level event pattern correlates with the observed retransmit behavior? Provider logs are still partial; follow-up with provider network ops needed.
- Was there an internal egress IP reallocation that coincided with the flap and exacerbated impact? Investigating infra change logs.
- Should we treat heavy-tenant egress pinning as a configuration anti-pattern and proactively reconfigure existing tenants? (Product tradeoff discussion needed.)

Oncall notes (for future responders):
- When streaming degradations occur, parallelize: check application-layer metrics AND immediately query edge.tcp.* metrics and provider BGP/session statuses. Do not assume internal scheduler bug first.
- Use the traffic-fallback automation (when available) in small stages first (10% -> 30%) and observe reconnect rates.
- If autoscaler triggers while packet loss is present, hold scaling and escalate. Scaling often amplifies KV-cache churn.

Appendix — useful commands and dashboards (draft):
- Dashboards: streaming/edges/us-west-2: token-latency-p95,p99; tcp/retransmit-rate; kv-cache/eviction-rate.
- Diagnostic commands (edge host):
  * `tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp and host <client-ip> and dst port <stream-port>' -c 10000 -w /tmp/trace.pcap`
  * `edgectl metrics query --metric edge.tcp.retransmit.rate --window 5m --group-by egress_ip,node`
  * `edgectl routing override --egress-set alternate-usw2 --duration 30m --staged 10,30,100`

Postmortem tone / distribution:
- This is a working draft; internal distribution to eng-sre, infra, network and product. After owners confirm action items, we will produce a customer-facing condensed summary.

Notes to self: check infra change log for 2029-10-12 02:00–03:30 UTC window for any egress-ip allocation or edge config rollouts.

End of document.

Autoscaler safety gate based on network loss signals
